title: ParseForm advice writes Request.Form/PostForm on every call, racing with concurrent form readers (even with IAST disabled)
claim: The woven deferred closure unconditionally re-assigns r.Form and r.PostForm on every ParseForm call, including the read-only no-op re-parse of an already-parsed request. In plain Go a defensive re-parse concurrent with FormValue/PostFormValue/r.Form reads is race-free; woven, it is a data race (reproduced with IAST enabled and with config.Enabled=false). Independent evidence for the secondary remark in life-lazy-reader-F1; distinct write site.
repro_command: cd iast/integration/testapp && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -race -run '^TestRaceHuntParseFormReparse' -count=3 -v .  # woven: 3 DATA RACE (logs/woven_parseform_woven.out, logs/woven_parseform_disabled.out); plain control: RACEHUNT_PLAIN=1 go test -race -run TestRaceHunt -count=3 -cpu=4,16 . -> races=0 (logs/plain_integ_control.out)

title: Store owner acquisition drops most concurrent request begins on ownerMu.TryLock contention even when permits and owner slots are free
claim: Manager.Acquire wins a permit, then store.Acquire fails on global ownerMu.TryLock contention and the request becomes DecisionCapacityDropped despite free capacity; 16 concurrent Begin/Finish loops (cap 64) lose 39-80% of begins, all attributable to store acquire drops.

title: TestCommitTaintedSkippedDedup is flaky under repeated runs
claim: The test asserts 2 distinct aggregated telemetry log records; aggregation depends on heartbeat/flush timing, so 1 of 60 runs saw 3 distinct records with the correct total count of 3.
